title: Unified patient workflow
summary: Four disconnected systems and a clipboard became one continuous flow — intake to follow-up, with nothing re-typed along the way.
challenge: Patient details were captured on paper at reception, re-typed into a practice management system, copied again into a separate billing tool and chased by phone for follow-ups. Every hand-off added delay and risk.
Clinicians were spending more time on admin than with patients, and roughly one in five follow-ups was missed entirely.
approach: We shadowed reception, clinical and billing teams across three sites to map the real journey — including the workarounds that never made it into any process document.
A clickable prototype of the new flow was tested with staff in week three, and each workflow shipped to a single pilot site before rolling out to the group.
solution: A single care-operations platform where intake is captured once and carried forward. Triage scores cases automatically, care plans pre-fill from history and consent, and every discharge schedules its own follow-up with escalation rules.
Role-based views give reception, clinicians and billing exactly what they need — all from the same record.
highlights: Digital intake with validation and consent capture
Rule-based triage with self-ordering queues
Care plans pre-filled from patient history
Automated follow-ups that escalate after 72 hours
Integration with existing billing and calendar systems

title: Real-time operations hub
summary: Three disconnected tools replaced by one live view of orders, inventory and revenue — so the morning stand-up stops being an archaeology session.
outcome: Problem → Dashboard → Single source of truth
challenge: Orders lived in the storefront, stock in a warehouse system and revenue in a finance spreadsheet updated weekly. Every decision started with an hour of exporting and reconciling data.
Stock-outs on best-sellers were spotted days late, and nobody trusted the numbers enough to act on them.
approach: We traced every metric the leadership team relied on back to its source, agreed a single definition for each, and designed the dashboard around the decisions it needed to support.
Event streams from the storefront and warehouse were normalized into one data model with near real-time sync.
solution: A live operations hub showing orders, inventory, fulfillment and growth in one place — with alerts for stock thresholds, fulfillment delays and revenue anomalies.
Drill-downs let any team move from a headline number to the individual orders behind it in two clicks.

title: Intelligent support pipeline
summary: Incoming queries are classified, routed and answered before a human opens the queue — and the ones that need a person arrive with context attached.
challenge: A small support team was drowning in repetitive questions — order status, refunds, stock availability — while complex cases waited hours in the same queue.
Average first response time had crept past four hours, and customer satisfaction scores were falling month on month.
approach: We analyzed six months of tickets to find the handful of intents that covered most of the volume, then built an evaluation set from real conversations before choosing any model.
Confidence thresholds decide what is answered automatically and what is routed to a person — with the full context pre-attached.
solution: An AI triage pipeline that classifies every incoming message, pulls order, account and history data, and either resolves it instantly or routes it to the right specialist with a drafted reply.
A review console lets the team correct answers in one click, feeding the evaluation set every week so accuracy keeps climbing.
highlights: Intent classification tuned on six months of real tickets
Retrieval over orders, policies and product catalog
Confidence thresholds with human-in-the-loop routing
Drafted replies with full customer context attached
Weekly evaluation runs to track accuracy drift

title: Legacy ERP modernization
summary: A 15-year-old ERP modernized piece by piece — faster, cheaper to run and ready for new products, without a single minute of downtime.
challenge: The manufacturer's ERP ran on an unsupported framework and a single on-premise server. Screens took seconds to load, every change risked breaking something else, and only one engineer understood the codebase.
A full rewrite had been quoted at two years — time the business simply didn't have.
approach: We mapped modules by business value and risk, wrapped critical flows in characterization tests and introduced an API layer in front of the legacy database.
New services replaced old modules one at a time using the strangler pattern, each released behind feature flags.
solution: A modern, containerized platform on managed cloud infrastructure, with a redesigned interface for the most-used screens and a clean API for future integrations.
Monitoring, automated deployments and documentation mean the in-house team now ships changes weekly instead of quarterly.

API layer in front of the legacy database

title: Boardly: real-time issue tracking
summary: A Kanban board and issue tracker that syncs every movement, edit, and comment in real time, while maintaining a comprehensive history for every ticket.
outcome: Scattered updates → Live board → One shared picture
challenge: Small teams run projects across chat threads, spreadsheets and a tracker nobody keeps current. By the time the weekly check-in starts, half the board is already out of date.

The tools they tested were either designed for massive organizations or lacked the two essential features they consistently requested: real-time updates visible to everyone and a transparent log tracking individual contributions.
approach: We started from the change, not the screen. Every move, edit and comment is written once, stored in the ticket's history and broadcast to everyone viewing that board.
The API came first, with typed request and response models, so the board, the list view and notifications all read from one contract.
Roles were settled before the first screen: owners manage boards and members, members move and discuss the work.
solution: Boardly pairs a Next.js front end with a FastAPI and PostgreSQL back end. Boards update live over WebSockets, so a card dragged on one screen moves on every other open screen within a second.
Each ticket carries its comments, watchers and a full audit history. Watchers are notified about the changes they care about, and the list view filters, sorts and searches across every board.
highlights: Drag-and-drop Kanban with live updates over WebSockets
Owner and member roles with board-level permissions
Complete change history on every ticket
Watchers with change notifications
List view with filters, sorting and search
Light and dark themes

title: DocuMind: answers from your documents
summary: Upload a PDF, Word file or slide deck and ask it anything. Every answer comes back with the page or slide it came from, so nobody has to take the AI's word for it.
outcome: Long documents → RAG assistant → Cited answers
challenge: Policies, contracts and decks run to dozens of pages, and the answer someone needs is usually one sentence in the middle. Search finds keywords, not answers.
General-purpose AI chat makes it worse: it answers confidently without saying where the answer came from a non-starter for HR, legal and compliance work.
approach: Each file type gets its own parser, so page numbers in PDFs, tables in Word files and speaker notes in slides survive the trip into the index.
Text is split into overlapping chunks, embedded with an open sentence-transformer model and stored in a FAISS index, so retrieval runs locally and fast.
The model may only answer from the passages retrieved, and must cite each one it uses. When nothing relevant comes back, it says so instead of guessing.
solution: DocuMind is a Python service with a chat interface: upload a PDF, DOCX or PPTX, ask a question in plain language, and get a short answer with numbered citations to the exact page or slide.
It runs on open models, all-mpnet-base-v2 for embeddings and Mistral 7B for answers so it can be hosted privately for documents that shouldn't leave the company.
highlights: PDF, DOCX and PPTX parsing that keeps page and slide numbers
Overlapping chunks for answers that span paragraphs
Local FAISS vector search with mpnet embeddings
Answers grounded only in retrieved passages
Numbered citations on every answer
Open models that can run on private infrastructure

title: CLEAR: an AI inbox for your head
summary: Type whatever is on your mind and let go. CLEAR turns each dump into tasks in the background and hands you three things to focus on every morning.
outcome: Mental clutter → AI inbox → A daily Top 3
challenge: To-do apps ask you to organize before you've finished a thought: pick a project, a due date, a priority, a label. So the thoughts stay in your head instead.
The result is a long list nobody trusts, and mornings spent deciding what to do rather than doing it.
approach: We wrote three rules before any design: dump, don't manage; the backend decides and the frontend obeys; one screen per mode.

A background worker reads each dump and turns it into tasks with dates and effort, using Gemini when a key is configured and a simple one-dump-one-task rule when it isn't — so the app never stops working.
Every screen was designed phone-first, for one thumb and a few seconds of attention.
solution: CLEAR is a React front end on a lightweight TypeScript API. There's one box to dump into, a background brain that sorts what you wrote, and a Daily Focus screen that picks your Top 3 each morning or on demand.
Lists, filters and settings stay out of the way until you go looking for them.

Background worker that turns dumps into tasks
Daily Top 3, picked every morning or on demand
Gemini task extraction with a no-AI fallback

One screen per mode, designed for one thumb

title: Re-platforming a legacy LMS
summary: A 2022 PHP learning portal, moved to Next.js and a typed API one module at a time — old and new side by side, with no big-bang cutover.
outcome: Legacy PHP → Module by module → No big-bang cutover
challenge: Our 2022 learning portal — institute, faculty and student dashboards in plain PHP — still did its job, but every change risked breaking another page. SQL lived inside the templates, sessions handled sign-in, and each dashboard was effectively its own app.
A full rewrite would have frozen the product for months. The goal was a modern platform without ever switching everything over in one night.
approach: We listed every PHP page with the module it belongs to and the data it touches, then put a typed API in front of the existing database so old and new screens read the same records.
Modules move one at a time, smallest risk first: sign-in, then students, timetables, study material and queries. A routing layer sends each path to the old app or the new one.
Every move ships behind a switch that can send traffic back to the PHP page in seconds.
solution: The new platform is one Next.js app with role-based views for the institute, faculty and students, backed by a typed Node.js API and deployed in containers alongside the legacy app.
Timetables update without a reload, study material is served from object storage through signed links, and student queries move out of email and into the app.
highlights: Page-by-page inventory of the legacy app
Typed API in front of the existing database
Routing layer that sends each path to old or new
One app with institute, faculty and student views
Instant rollback switch for every module
